description: Field Shift is an AI-powered agricultural decision-support platform that combines NASA Earth observation data with local soil information, crop characteristics, and farmer priorities. It analyzes temperature, rainfall, soil moisture, and vegetation patterns to identify agricultural risks and compare existing and alternative crop rotation strategies. Through interactive visualizations and explainable recommendations Field Shift helps farmers explore sustainable farming practices and improve soil.
summary:
Field Shift: Crop-Rotation Decision Support from NASA Earth Observations

Field Shift is a bilingual (English and Urdu) web platform that helps farmers in Punjab, Pakistan, evaluate crop rotations for water use, soil health and climate resilience. Each rotation is tested against 25 years of NASA Earth observation data.

The platform uses the following NASA datasets:

NASA POWER daily weather, downloaded live for any location a user selects on the map
MODIS vegetation index and land cover
SMAP soil moisture
GPM IMERG precipitation, used to independently check the POWER rainfall
SRTM elevation, used to assess slope and erosion risk
The analysis applies FAO-56 crop water requirements, FAO-29 salinity thresholds and heat-stress indicators. Each rotation receives six suitability scores, weighted by the farmer's own priorities. A ridge-regression model, validated year by year, forecasts crop greenness six weeks ahead. Results also include daily Punjab AMIS market prices and a seven-day weather forecast. Users can save a plan and share it as a link.
details:
Field Shift: Crop-Rotation Decision Support from NASA Earth Observations

Field Shift is a bilingual (English and Urdu) web platform that helps farmers in Punjab, Pakistan, evaluate crop rotations for water use, soil health and climate resilience. Each rotation is tested against 25 years of NASA Earth observation data.

The platform uses the following NASA datasets:

NASA POWER daily weather, downloaded live for any location a user selects on the map

MODIS vegetation index and land cover

SMAP soil moisture

GPM IMERG precipitation, used to independently check the POWER rainfall

SRTM elevation, used to assess slope and erosion risk

The analysis applies FAO-56 crop water requirements, FAO-29 salinity thresholds and heat-stress indicators. Each rotation receives six suitability scores, weighted by the farmer's own priorities. A ridge-regression model, validated year by year, forecasts crop greenness six weeks ahead. Results also include daily Punjab AMIS market prices and a seven-day weather forecast. Users can save a plan and share it as a link.

Field Shift is built with Next.js, TypeScript and a PostgreSQL database, and runs on Vercel. Its scientific engine was checked against an independent Python reference implementation on 480 rotation evaluations, and the results matched exactly. A suite of 143 automated tests runs on every change.

Field Shift is intended to support, not replace, the guidance of local agricultural extension officers.

Live platform: https://fieldshiftmain.vercel.app

Source code: https://github.com/HassanCodes-max/fieldshiftmain
